finding: Customer tenure is the strongest churn-related numerical factor
result: Churned customers: 17.98 months average tenure; non-churned customers: 37.57 months
business_implication: Prioritize retention and engagement during the early stages of the customer lifecycle

finding: Contract type is moderately associated with churn
result: Month-to-month customers have substantially higher churn than customers on longer-term contracts
business_implication: Investigate financially sustainable strategies to encourage migration to longer-term contracts

finding: Internet service is moderately associated with churn
result: Fiber optic customers show substantially higher churn than DSL and customers without internet service
business_implication: Investigate service quality, pricing, technical issues, and customer expectations among Fiber optic customers

finding: Payment method is moderately associated with churn
result: Electronic check customers show substantially higher churn than customers using other payment methods
business_implication: Investigate payment friction, customer characteristics, and pricing among Electronic check customers

finding: Monthly Charges are associated with churn but have a smaller effect
result: Churned customers average 74.44 in Monthly Charges versus 61.27 among non-churned customers
business_implication: Consider pricing alongside contract, service, and tenure rather than treating it as a standalone churn explanation

finding: Total Charges should not be treated as a primary churn driver
result: Total Charges differ significantly between churned and non-churned customers, but the effect is smaller than tenure
business_implication: Use Total Charges as a measure of customer value and history rather than evidence that accumulated spending causes churn

finding: Monthly Charges differ substantially by Internet Service
result: Internet Service explains a large proportion of the variation in Monthly Charges
business_implication: Interpret pricing differences in the context of the service customers receive

finding: Monthly Charges differ by Payment Method
result: Payment Method has a large effect on Monthly Charges
business_implication: Consider payment structure when evaluating pricing-related churn patterns

finding: Tenure and Total Charges have a strong positive relationship
result: Longer-tenured customers tend to have higher accumulated Total Charges
business_implication: Total Charges should be interpreted together with tenure rather than as an independent churn factor
